claims.claim: In a 12-month real-world test of seven Aqara motion sensors, six of seven exceeded the manufacturer's claimed ~1-year battery life.

claims.quote: All sensors used fresh CR2032 coin cells (225mAh capacity), reported door/window state every 30 seconds, and logged voltage every 10 minutes. End of life was defined as voltage dropping below 2.0V (sensor shutdown). Test duration: 12 months, all 120 sensors completed the test with no hardware failures.
claims.claim: A controlled 12-month benchmark of 120 sensors (40 each Zigbee 3.0, Z-Wave 800, Wi-Fi 6) on CR2032 cells, reporting every 30 seconds, with voltage-based end-of-life detection.
At 30-second reporting intervals, measured battery life was 14.3 months (Zigbee 3.0), 18.2 months (Z-Wave 800), and only 4.3 months (Wi-Fi 6) on CR2032.
Halving reporting to 60 seconds roughly doubled measured battery life: 22.7 months (Zigbee), 28.5 months (Z-Wave), 7.1 months (Wi-Fi).

claims.quote: Zigbee 3.0 battery life dropped by 18% (14.3 to 11.7 months) due to retransmissions, Z-Wave 800 saw no drop (18.2 months) as 908MHz is unaffected by 2.4GHz interference
claims.claim: Under heavy 2.4 GHz interference, measured Zigbee battery life dropped 18% (to 11.7 months) due to retransmissions, while Z-Wave was unaffected.

claims.quote: For industrial environments with heavy 2.4GHz interference (e.g., factories with 50+ Wi-Fi devices), Zigbee battery life dropped to 8.1 months, while Z-Wave remained at 17.9 months.
claims.claim: In extreme 2.4 GHz noise, measured Zigbee battery life fell to 8.1 months—nearly half the clean-environment figure—showing environment matters as much as protocol.

claims.quote: outside of this test, I've been running first-gen Aqara sensors in my own home for years without a battery change. They are among the most efficient Zigbee temperature and humidity sensors out there, even though they run on a single CR2032 battery.
claims.claim: A reviewer running first-gen Aqara Zigbee temperature sensors reports multiple years without a battery swap on a single CR2032, corroborating thesmarthomebook's 2-year data.

claims.quote: Paulie ● deserves a specific mention here too. Its CR2477 packs meaningfully more capacity than a standard CR2032, at the cost of just a bit of extra thickness. Its official rated battery life is 4 years, the best in this comparison.
claims.claim: The SONOFF SNZB-02P Zigbee temperature sensor carries a 4-year official battery rating (CR2477), though the reviewer notes they did not independently verify this in the test.

claims.quote: SONOFF claims up to 5 years, but we know it really depends on usage.
claims.claim: SONOFF claims 5-year battery life for the SNZB-04P Zigbee door sensor, but the reviewer cautions that real-world results depend heavily on usage patterns.

no_source: A long-term (multi-year) real-world battery study specifically for Bluetooth LE (BLE) smart home sensors (e.g., Xiaomi Mijia BLE, Govee BLE, SwitchBot BLE) with measured remaining capacity over time. All field data found was for Zigbee sensors; BLE sensor longevity data is only available via manufacturer claims or very short-term reviews.

claims.quote: We developed a conversational agent to help children with ADHD initiate and complete tasks. In this work, we investigate whether the conversational agent can help create regularity in children's lives.
claims.claim: This is the study most directly on-topic — a conversational agent built specifically to support task initiation and completion in children with ADHD.

claims.quote: a field test was conducted by five elementary school teachers in their private homes with their children with non-ADHD for eight days.
claims.claim: The actual testing was done with only five children, none of whom had ADHD, so the study provides essentially no direct evidence of benefit for ADHD users — it is a prototype feasibility evaluation only.

claims.claim: Qualitative feedback from one parent (of a non-ADHD child) suggested the agent helped with initiating a morning routine, a task-initiation-relevant anecdote — but again, not in a diagnosed ADHD sample.

claims.quote: NUROW, which consists of Go/No-go Task- and N-Back/Updating-based training modules and a personalized adaptive algorithm system that adjusts the difficulty level according to the user's performance, was implemented on 30 Korean children with ADHD aged 6 to 12 years.
claims.claim: A digital therapeutic with an adaptive algorithm (executive-function training, not a conversational assistant) was tested in children with diagnosed ADHD.

claims.quote: The ARS inattention (F = 4.080, p = 0.010), hyperactivity (F = 5.998. p < 0.001), and sum (F = 5.902, p < 0.001) significantly improved.
claims.claim: ADHD symptom ratings improved significantly after four weeks of the executive-function digital therapeutic, though the study was a single-group feasibility design with no control condition.

claims.quote: Forty adults with ADHD were randomised, of whom 17 participants in each group completed self-guided psychoeducation based on either a chatbot or conventional psychoeducation app between October 2020 and July 2021.
claims.claim: A small RCT tested a chatbot intervention in adults with diagnosed ADHD — one of the few randomized studies of any chatbot in this population.

claims.quote: Self-guided psychoeducation based on a chatbot or a conventional app appears similarly effective and safe for improving ADHD core symptoms.
claims.claim: The chatbot improved ADHD core symptoms about as much as a conventional app, but since both groups improved equally and there was no non-treatment control, the benefit can't be attributed to the AI/chatbot format specifically, and the intervention was psychoeducation rather than task-initiation support.

claims.claim: The generative AI tool showed non-significant trends toward better task completion and engagement in ADHD students — suggestive but not statistically demonstrated benefit.

claims.claim: ADHD students in the pilot qualitatively reported that the GenAI scaffolding helped specifically with task initiation and planning.
